'''Jordan Williams''' (born October 11, 1990) is a basketball player.  He played two seasons of [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Maryland]] [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Terrapins men's basketball]] team.  

==High school career==
Williams played high school basketball for [[Torrington High School]] in [[Torrington, Connecticut]].  He averaged 36 points a game as a senior in high school.<ref name=bsun20Feb2010>{{cite news|last=Markus|first=Don|title=Maryland's Williams exceeds expectations|url=http://articles.baltimoresun.com/2010-02-20/sports/bal-sp.terpshoop20feb20_1_greivis-vasquez-jordan-williams-gary-williams/2|accessdate=22 January 2011|newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|date=20 February 2010}}</ref>   Due to questions about the level of his competition, Williams did not receive heavy publicity or recruiting attention in high school.<ref name=bsun20Feb2010 /><ref name=washpost18Nov2010>{{cite news|last=Clarke|first=Liz|title=Jordan Williams, Maryland basketball ready for first true challenge of the season|url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2010/11/17/AR2010111706352.html?sid=ST2010111706692|accessdate=22 January 2011|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=18 November 2010}}</ref>

==College career==
Williams committed to [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] on October 21, 2008.

===Freshman===
Williams started 31 games as a freshman for the [[2009–10 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team]].  He was an All-ACC rookie team selection.  Williams finished second in rebounding in [[2009–10 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|the ACC]].<ref name=umterps>{{cite web|title=Player Bio: Jordan Williams|url=http://www.umterps.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/williams_jordan00.html|work=UMTerps.com|accessdate=22 January 2011}}</ref>   Maryland coach [[Gary Williams]] complimented Williams' growth as a player as the season progressed.<ref name=bsun20Feb2010 />

===Sophomore===
Before his sophomore season, Williams was named  to the preseason watch list for the [[Wooden Award]] and [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Award]] watchlists.<ref name=washpost18Nov2010 />   In a January 22, 2011 victory over [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]], Williams recorded his thirteenth straight [[Double-double]], which set a Maryland record.  He broke a streak previously held by [[Len Elmore]].<ref name=wpost22Jan2011>{{cite news|last=Clarke|first=Liz|title=Maryland vs. Clemson: Late free throws help Terrapins hold off Tigers|url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2011/01/22/AR2011012202981.html|accessdate=22 January 2011|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=22 January 2011}}</ref> He was picked to the Third Team All-America by [[Fox Sports]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Goodman|url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711|title=Goodman's 2010-11 All-America teams|work=[[Fox Sports]]||publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media|date=Mar 7, 2011|accessdate=June 21, 2011}}</ref>

After the season, Williams submitted his name to the NBA draft.  Initially, he did not sign with an agent, which left open the possibility of staying in college.<ref name=wpost29Mar2011>{{cite news|last=Clarke|first=Liz|title=Maryland’s Jordan Williams submits for NBA draft|url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/marylands-jordan-williams-submits-for-nba-draft/2011/03/29/AFskhgyB_story.html|accessdate=30 March 2011|newspaper=[[Washington Post]]|date=29 March 2011}}</ref>  He later hired an agent, which precluded a return to collegiate basketball.<ref name=csnwash>{{cite web|last=Standig|first=Benjamin|title=Jordan Williams going pro|url=http://www.csnwashington.com/05/04/11/Jordan-Williams-going-pro/landing.html?blockID=516616&feedID=276|work=[[Comcast Sports Net{{!}}CSN Washington]]|accessdate=6 May 2011}}</ref>
